evidence: deepseek: `if p1 + p2 > T` followed by `if p1_sum > T`; gpt-oss: `if p1 + p2 > T` followed by total-load checks; qwen: `Check if any single job exceeds T`; glm-5: `Check for JOB violation first`
affordance_in_statement: `JOB i` — the i-th item ... requires a sequential chain of operations whose combined duration strictly exceeds the shift length; `LOAD c` — the equipment at stage c ... is assigned a total active duration across all items that strictly exceeds the shift length.
removal_suggestion: Re-present certificate validity through an indirect schedule-accounting or audit-witness definition rather than explicitly describing the two tests as p1[i] + p2[i] > T and sum(p_c) > T. Keep the same labels and physical meaning, but require the solver to derive the relevant occupied intervals from the scenario.

common_affordance: The statement directly exposes that every accepted certificate is obtained by one of two scalar threshold tests: a single item's p1 + p2 versus T or a stage-wide sum versus T.
recommended_edit: Replace the explicit additive descriptions of JOB and LOAD validity with an indirect physical audit formulation: define validity in terms of the corresponding sequential occupation interval or machine-occupation ledger, requiring those quantities to be derived from the production scenario rather than handed to the solver as 'combined duration' and 'total active duration' threshold checks.
